fixes.explanation: The Pharisees were a Jewish group that shows up in the Gospels (Matthew 23:2). They aren't named in this letter. Jesus says it's "…the teaching of the Nicolaitans." (Revelation 2:15). Nice try, friend, but the Pharisees aren't on this page.

True. Jesus says, "Otherwise I will come to you shortly and wage war against them with the sword of My mouth." (Revelation 2:16). He says "them," and the text doesn't spell out who that is, so I'll leave it there. And remember who opened this letter, the One with the sharp, double-edged sword (Revelation 2:12).

It's actually in the text. Jesus says, "Otherwise I will come to you shortly and wage war against them with the sword of My mouth." (Revelation 2:16). He says "them," and the text doesn't say who that is. Right before it, He says, "Therefore repent!" (Revelation 2:16).

Yes! Jesus says, "I will also give him a white stone inscribed with a new name, known only to the one who receives it." (Revelation 2:17). A stone with a new name on it, and only the one who gets it knows that name. That's a gift made for one person.

Stone with writing on it, so I see the connection, friend. But this white stone is "…inscribed with a new name, known only to the one who receives it." (Revelation 2:17). The text names a new name on it, not a list of rules.
Right. Jesus says the new name is "…known only to the one who receives it." (Revelation 2:17). So the rest of the church doesn't know it. Only the one who gets the stone does.
That's right. Jesus says, "…your latest deeds are greater than your first." (Revelation 2:19). Their latest deeds are greater than their first. That's a church still growing, and He notices.
Jesus doesn't say that to Thyatira. He says, "…your latest deeds are greater than your first." (Revelation 2:19). Greater, not weaker. Good news for Thyatira.
Jesus doesn't say flat or the same. He says, "…your latest deeds are greater than your first." (Revelation 2:19). Their latest deeds are greater than their first. Keep going, Thyatira!

I'd love that ending, baker. But Jesus says, "Even though I have given her time to repent of her immorality, she is unwilling." (Revelation 2:21). The text says she is unwilling, not that she repents. It doesn't report a repentance in this passage.

Nothing like that in this letter. Jesus says, "…I am the One who searches minds and hearts…" (Revelation 2:23). That's what all the churches will know about Him. Favoring the oldest churches isn't in the text.

That's the word. Jesus says, "…than to hold fast to what you have until I come." (Revelation 2:25). It's what He told them to hold onto, until He comes. That's why I keep my ovens warm, baker. I just never guess when.

Good guess, since prophets show up all over the Bible, but not here. Jesus says, "…just as I have received authority from My Father." (Revelation 2:27). His authority comes from the Father, and that's the answer.

I get why people go there, baker, but no. Jesus says, "…just as I have received authority from My Father." (Revelation 2:27). His authority comes from the Father, not from people. The Father is the source.
